title: Redis Distributed Caching for AI Workloads
description: Implement Redis distributed caching for AI response caching, embedding storage, and rate-limit state coordination across scaled instances.

data.text: Why Distributed Caching is Critical for AI Applications

AI workloads are expensive — both in compute and cost. A distributed cache (Redis) shared across all application instances provides three critical benefits: (1) semantic response caching prevents duplicate LLM calls, (2) embedding caching avoids redundant vector computation, and (3) rate-limit state coordination ensures consistent quota management across scaled instances.

Semantic caching stores responses keyed not by exact prompt match, but by semantic similarity. If a new query is semantically similar to a cached prompt, the cached response is returned. This is especially powerful for FAQ-style queries or knowledge base lookups, reducing LLM costs by 50-80%.

data.text: When horizontally scaling AI services across multiple instances, each instance must share rate-limit state. Redis atomic increment operations with sliding window counters provide consistent rate limiting across all instances, preventing quota violations from race conditions.

data.text: Use Redis Streams for audit logging of AI interactions. Each LLM call, token count, and user ID can be streamed to a Redis Stream, which is consumed by monitoring services for cost tracking and abuse detection.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: LLM response caching, embedding caching, and rate-limit coordination are the three primary AI caching use cases
Semantic caching uses vector similarity to match near-duplicate prompts, saving 50-80% on LLM costs
Distributed rate limiters must use atomic Redis operations to coordinate across scaled instances
Set appropriate TTLs: responses 1-7 days, embeddings 1-30 days, rate limits per-minute
Redis Streams can audit log all AI interactions for cost tracking and abuse detection
data.takeaway: Distributed caching is the bridge from single-instance development to multi-instance production for AI applications — it directly affects cost, performance, and scalability.
